Actors:
Local/regional Key individuals within the regional industrial system with the ability and energy to engage
champions others, push for and broaden IS participation among firms.

Organisational Key individuals within an organization that can get others interested in the concept and that
champions can secure support for the identified opportunities.

Physical anchors Actors that control large and stable resource flows around which new synergies can
develop.

Institutional Actors with the possibility to bring actors together to facilitate interaction, to provide
anchors education, to give development, financial and policy support, and to legitimize and
disseminate learned lessons.

Coordinators Actors that can oversee and drive diverse range of activities needed to realise symbiotic
practices.

Brokers Facilitate transactions between other actors who lack access to, or trust in, on another.
Brokers can be sub-divided into relationship-, information-, and knowledge-brokers

Relationship Actors helping others who are interested in collaboration but who lack experience,
brokers knowledge or contact with other interested firms by making introductions.

Information Actors collecting information on what different actors need and can offer, in order to
brokers identify compatibilities and inform relevant parties about potential options.

Knowledge Actors who can fill knowledge gaps by providing knowledge directly or through connections
providers/brokers to other holders of knowledge.

Technical system Actors who own and operate systems for transferring and processing energy, water and
operators material resources.
Regenerators Actors specialised in creating value from residuals and wastes.
